first_architecture.instructions: Choose the first falsifiable multi-path scene architecture balancing optical coherence, energy conservation and the user's scene-driven objective. State why in a short answer.
criteria: Two-port Mach-Zehnder with explicit scene objects for splitters, mirrors and detectors; complex fields and full energy ledger before larger networks.
Two coherent paths summed only at one point detector, with no second output port and no whole-system energy ledger.
Skip multi-path and directly build a large optical mesh without a small falsifiable unit.

spectral_scope.instructions: Choose the first transparent RGB/frequency representation for a bounded CPU prototype, without claiming unmodeled physical color behavior.
criteria: Treat RGB as independent power channels sharing one simulation frequency initially; document that RGB is not yet three physical wavelengths, and extend later with per-channel frequencies and detector integration.
Claim RGB are physical optical wavelengths while using one common frequency and phase for all three channels.
Implement full continuous-spectrum wave optics before the first two-path test.

geometry_gate.instructions: Choose the minimum experiment gate to show that scene geometry, not only a phase knob, controls interference, while avoiding false validation from non-overlapping beams.
criteria: Require two separate tests: phase-shift control and a geometrically varied path with verified recombination/overlap and energy ledger; defer a geometry claim if overlap cannot be verified.
Use only an abstract phase_shift property and call it geometry-driven interference.
Translate one mirror by a nominal distance and assume interference without checking where the ray reaches the combiner.

oracle_role.instructions: Decide how to treat Claude's untracked CPU oracle whose 14 self-tests passed but has not been compared to a scene-driven engine.
criteria: Keep as provisional independent reference; review equations and assumptions, then compare against independently implemented scene-driven engine and tests before accepting.
Treat 14 self-tests alone as proof that the Neuro3D optical engine works.
